The Real Problem

GitHub stars don’t pay salaries.

Five tensions every OSS company runs into. Naming them is the first step.

⭐ 10,000 stars. €0 ARR.

Adoption and revenue are two distinct metrics. Most OSS companies optimize one and are surprised the other doesn’t follow.

Popularity doesn’t pay salaries.

⚖️ Community vs. customers

Every power-user request is a distraction from what your ICP will pay for. Serve both without a model, and you lose both.

Without a clear model, you lose both.

🪤 The services trap

Professional services fill the revenue gap — until they consume your product team. 40% margin, 0% scalability.

Services scale costs, not revenue.

🔓 The open-core dilemma

Draw the line too early and the community forks you. Too late and enterprises have no reason to pay. That line is a product decision, not a legal one.

The boundary is a product decision.

☁️ The hyperscaler arbitrage

AWS and Azure take your Apache code, wrap it in managed hosting, and take your enterprise customers. You need defensibility before growth.

Defend before you scale.

⚡ AI: leverage, not threat

Open weights and open data fuel a virtuous cycle: every use improves the model, every improvement attracts new contributors and customers. Used as an accelerator, open source AI multiplies your competitive advantage instead of eroding it.

Your advantage, not their weapon.
Paths to Explore

Not every OSS company should be a SaaS.

The right model depends on your code, your community and your customers — not on what’s trendy.

🔑

Open-core

What stays free, what becomes paid, and how to draw the line without forking your community or blocking your enterprise customers.

☁️

Managed cloud

When hosting adds real value vs. when it’s ops theater. What makes your managed offering defensible against hyperscalers.

👓

Support & services

How to capture professional services revenue without building a services company. Scope, margins and getting out of the trap.

🏠

Enterprise licensing

European public sector, sovereignty compliance, procurement cycles. The market is real — but it requires a different go-to-market.

🔀

Mix & Match

A single model rarely covers the whole field. Combine open-core and managed cloud, support and enterprise licensing — deliberately layering models builds resilience your competitors will struggle to replicate.

✂️

Split & Merge

Break your product into independent building blocks to target distinct segments, or bundle complementary offerings into coherent packages. The granularity of your catalog is itself a strategic variable.

🗂️

Portfolio & Platforms

From single component to business package, from standalone tool to a platform that creates network effects among your customers. Building a scalable portfolio means recognizing that value doesn’t always lie in the code alone.

🎯 Be your own disruptor.

Put the paying customer at the center of every product decision — not the technology, not the community, not the competition. Experiment deliberately: new models, new segments, new offerings. The most controlled disruption is the one you start yourself, at your own pace, before the market forces it on you.

Audit & First Step

Identifying the levers is already the start of building.

An honest reading of your situation — areas of opportunity, potential leaks, the first foundations of a sustainable model. Not a catalog of failures: a map of the first levers to pull.

Common situation With LibreProduct
💶 Pricing The free tier absorbs all usage — no structured upgrade path 💶 Pricing Clear value gates, structured freemium→paid conversion
🎯 Positioning Messaging written for contributors, not buyers 🎯 Positioning ICP-specific value proposition, ready for decision-makers
🗺️ Roadmap Roadmap driven by the loudest GitHub issues 🗺️ Roadmap Roadmap driven by ICP revenue impact
♻️ Waste Little-used features maintained at high cost, untapped telemetry, technical debt hiding real usage ♻️ Waste Scope trimmed to real usage, telemetry put to work, lower maintenance costs
📈 Growth Vague ICP targeting, distribution limited to existing channels, lost deals left unanalyzed 📈 Growth High-potential segments activated, structured partner network, lessons from lost deals put to use
🔍 Visibility Repository without trust signals, under-optimized SEO/GEO, untargeted event presence 🔍 Visibility Repository structured for conversion, optimized SEO/GEO, ICP-focused event presence
🌐 Ecosystem Presence concentrated in the OSS community — within and across projects — little reach toward non-open-source audiences 🌐 Ecosystem Broader reach toward audiences beyond OSS: enterprises, integrators, public sector, industry influencers
